page: Microsoft Azure D128lds_v6 is an x86_64 compute-oriented server instance utilizing dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processors capable of speeds up to 4.2 GHz. The platform provisions 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores via Hyper-V virtualization, supported by 260 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates 256 GB of system RAM, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio (2 GB per vCPU). An integrated 7,560 GB NVMe SSD volume provides high-capacity local storage. Discrete GPU acceleration is not present on this instance type.

Performance testing reflects high multi-core scalability and memory throughput. The system achieves top-tier results in PassMark CPU tests (103,274.51) and multi-threaded decompression (666.95 GB/sec), augmented by Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 501.02 GB/sec and write bandwidth measures 215.13 GB/sec. Real-world database and networking performance is notable, measuring 146.84 million Redis SET operations per second and 162.64 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The 2 GB of RAM per vCPU configuration trades per-core memory footprint for compute thread density. While prompt processing across language models performs strongly due to matrix extensions, single-threaded processing and small-model token generation remain moderate. The inclusion of 7,560 GB of local NVMe SSD provides significant qualitative cost efficiency by removing the necessity for secondary high-IOPS network storage when managing large local scratch disks, temporary indexes, or build outputs.

Microsoft Azure D128lds_v6 is designed for distributed continuous integration pipelines, multi-threaded code compilation, static web serving, high-throughput caching layers, and high-concurrency batch ETL workloads that require high CPU density and fast local ephemeral storage.
description: Microsoft Azure D128lds_v6 is a compute-dense instance powered by Intel Xeon 8573C processors running at up to 4.2 GHz, featuring 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores, 256 GB of memory, and 7,560 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage. The x86_64 architecture incorporates 260 MB of L3 cache alongside AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-tier multi-threaded capabilities, registering over 146 million Redis SET operations per second, 162.64 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, and memory read speeds exceeding 500 GB/sec. Although the 2 GB per vCPU memory allocation favors compute density over large-footprint in-memory caching, the bundled high-capacity NVMe array offers qualitative efficiency for high-IOPS applications. This instance is strategically configured for multi-threaded compilation, batch data transformation, high-concurrency web tiers, and ephemeral database caching.
